newsitem.title: CHILE: El Abra copper mine paralyzed by accident.
newsitem.headline: El Abra copper mine paralyzed by accident.

text.p: Work at the El Abra copper mine in northern Chile has been paralyzed by an accident caused by the collapse of a covering over a conveyor belt, a mine official said.
Four workers died in the accident when they they were buried under tonnes of earth and rocks, officials said.
"The conveyor belt carries the ore to the plant, so obviously production is absolutely stopped," said the mine's human resources manager, Rodrigo Salinas.
The mine was built by U.S. mining company Cyprus Amax Minerals in a joint venture with Chile's state copper firm Codelco,
"We have had 100 percent of labour staff dedicated to the rescue efforts," he told Reuters by telephone from the mine, owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals and Chilean state copper firm Codelco.
He said mine officials had no idea yet how much production would be lost due to the accident and that they would begin evaluating the effect on copper output on Thursday.
"Obviously, we have been worried about other things today," he said.
The mine, the world's largest heap leaching operation, made its first cathode in August but is not expected to reach full production of 225,000 tonnes of fine copper until 1997.
